title: Felix and the Detention
premise: Petra Marchetti has spent high school as 'the baker's kid,' invisible behind the counter of his family's shop, counting down to graduation. When he finds his late grandmother's recipe box, one card isn't a recipe at all — it's a set of instructions that pulls him into the Detention, a liminal school where people trapped by other people's labels are held until they forget who they were. To escape before the Detention's final game of the season seals its students forever, Petra must bake memories back into the lost souls around him — and confront which of his own labels he actually wants to keep. He wins his release by refusing to play the game on the Detention's terms, walks out with his grandmother's true legacy, and returns home to graduate as someone who chose his own name.
about_author: Ansel Quintana is a former night-shift baker from a rust-belt town who writes stories about kitchens, ghosts, and kids nobody bothers to learn the names of. This is his second novel for young adults.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Senior year grinds on; Petra rises at 4 a.m. to bake with his father, known to everyone only as 'the Marchetti boy.' At school he's a ghost in the yearbook photo — half out of frame. The emotional beat is quiet resentment: he loves baking but hates being an ingredient in other people's lives.

chapters.title: The Card That Isn't Bread
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Cleaning out grandma Rosa's things, Petra finds her recipe box and a card reading not flour and yeast but a list of instructions ending in 'stay until you remember.' Reading it aloud, the kitchen dissolves. The beat is wonder curdling into fear as he lands in a hallway that smells like every school he's ever dreaded.

chapters.title: Attendance Is Mandatory
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He meets the Detention's residents: kids and adults stuck mid-label — the Jock, the Burnout, the Teacher's Pet — all slowly forgetting their real names. A hall monitor called Proctor explains the rules: leave through the last game of the season, or stay forever. Beat: dread mixed with recognition.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Was a Role
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with flashbacks. He befriends Wren, labeled 'the Scholarship Kid,' who can't recall her mother's face but recites her GPA perfectly. Petra discovers his grandmother was once a resident here — and escaped. Beat: hope, and the first hint this place runs on memory like dough runs on yeast.

chapters.title: What the Ovens Remember
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the Detention's abandoned kitchen, Petra bakes using Rosa's cards and accidentally restores a resident's memory — the smell of cardamom brings back the Jock's real name, Marcus. Proctor notices. Beat: exhilaration followed by the cold understanding that the Detention feeds on forgotten selves.

chapters.title: Labels Off
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. He starts secretly baking for residents, peeling labels away one by one; the Detention begins to fray, hallways shortening. But Wren refuses his bread — terrified that without 'Scholarship Kid' she'll be nothing at all. Beat: painful mirror; Petra sees his own hiding inside hers.

chapters.title: Proctor's Offer
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Proctor reveals the truth: the Detention keeps people safe from the pain of being mislabeled out there, and offers Petra a permanent place — honored, needed, never 'the baker's kid' again. Tempted, he nearly accepts. Beat: the antagonist's argument almost lands because it's kind.

chapters.title: The Last Game
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Game day arrives; the field is the exit and the trap both. Residents must choose: play and belong here forever, or walk off the field unnamed into the world. Petra publicly bakes one loaf — Rosa's memory bread — and shares it with everyone willing to take it. Beat: open rebellion, rising stakes.

chapters.title: Rosa's Instructions
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax. Proctor tries to seal the doors mid-game; Petra realizes the final card's last line — 'stay until you remember' — meant him: he must fully claim who he is, baker and son and himself, not either/or. Naming himself aloud, he breaks the Detention's hold; it collapses into flour-white light. Beat: identity as the key.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, resolution. He wakes in the family kitchen; whether it was dream or elsewhere is left soft-edged, but Marcus and Wren find the shop weeks later, remembering. Petra puts his full name on the graduation program, bakes for the ceremony, and adds his own first recipe card to Rosa's box. Beat: belonging chosen, not assigned.
